title: Runtime call harmonizer with name rewriting and contract validation
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a runtime-level harmonizer that reconciles OpenAI-style tool descriptors with Redwood legacy function contracts. The harmonizer should expose: 1) deterministic name-rewriting rules with a canonical registry, 2) contract validation (schema-level) before invocation, 3) safe fallback behaviors when validation fails, and 4) light-weight telemetry to measure mismatches and auto-suggest mappings. This work is intended to reduce production errors when customers migrate from legacy function endpoints to OpenAI-style tools and to make the runtime resilient to name and schema drift.
motivation: Customers integrating third-party agents and older Redwood functions frequently hit errors from mismatched tool names and parameter schemas. These errors increase latency (retries), support burden, and cause inconsistent user-facing behavior. We need a runtime bridge to reduce friction and support gradual migrations without requiring widespread client changes.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical name registry with deterministic rewrite rules implemented and deployed behind feature flag
Schema-driven contract validator that runs pre-invocation and returns structured validation errors when mismatch occurs

Fallback policy: on validation failure, runtime evaluates: (a) best-effort param coercion, (b) mapped legacy function invocation, (c) safe abort with structured diagnostic output — all configurable per-tenant
End-to-end tests covering: exact name match, alias resolution, parameter coercion, and structured abort output
Telemetry: metrics emitted for name-resolution success/failure, validation error types, and fallback path taken
Performance: median added latency < 3ms for name resolution + validation on warm path, P99 < 12ms in worst-case paths
Feature flag rollout plan and canary targeting per-tenant; ability to emergency-disable the harmonizer without restart
Documentation: developer guide, runbook for operators, and migration checklist published (links in 'links' field)
tasks: spec: define canonical registry format and rewrite grammar (RFC) — PRD link in links
implement: name-rewrite module with deterministic matching & alias table
implement: JSON-schema based contract validator and error canonicalizer
implement: fallback engine with coercion rules and invocation router to legacy functions
tests: unit + integration harness simulating mixed OpenAI-tool and legacy function traffic
telemetry: add telemetry tags and dashboards for mismatch/repair rates
deploy: behind feature flag, staged canary rollout to internal tenants
docs: publish dev guide, migration checklist, and operator runbook
risks: Incorrect canonicalization rules could silently route calls to wrong functions — mitigated by conservative default and validation-only mode
Validation/coercion may introduce subtle semantic changes to inputs — mitigation: opt-in coercion and detailed telemetry
Latency regression for high-throughput tenants — mitigation: microbenchmarks, caching, and JITing registry lookups
Edge cases where third-party agents rely on non-deterministic name variations — mitigation: provide a manual alias override API and audit log

qa_plan: Unit tests for registry matching and name rewrite grammar
Property tests for contract validator and coercion routines
Integration tests that replay historical agent traffic with canary config
Performance tests that simulate 10k RPS per shard with common alias cache enabled
Fault injection tests: network partitions to legacy function endpoints and graceful fallback verification
migration_plan: Phase 0: validation-only mode for 2 internal tenants, collect telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 1: enable opt-in coercion and aliasing for select customers with assistance
Phase 2: offer a backfill/alias suggestion tool to ingest historical invocation logs and propose mappings
Phase 3: default on for new deployments after 90 days of stable telemetry and zero critical mismatches
notes_for_support: Provide a diagnostic dump command 'rw harmonizer:diag <tenant>' to capture registry, recent mismatches, and last fallback traces
When customers report 'unknown tool' errors, check harmonizer mismatch metric and advise enabling validation-only mode to gather diagnostics
Use backfill tool to generate alias suggestions; always require customer approval before automatic alias creation
